headline: Iran conflict and yield surge push sentiment from greed toward fear
body: Wednesday's premarket tape is soft but not disorderly — Dow futures off roughly 0.15%, S&P 500 futures down about 0.2%, and Nasdaq-100 futures lagging near -0.5% — after Tuesday's session saw the Dow drop more than 400 points on fresh US strikes against Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude jumped roughly 5% to near $95 a barrel, its highest since late July, while the 10-year Treasury yield climbed to about 4.78%, its highest level since January 2025, as energy-driven inflation fears reinforced already-hawkish Fed rhetoric. Futures markets are pricing roughly 60% odds of a September rate hike, though Goldman Sachs is pushing back, arguing the Fed holds steady through year-end. Tech and chip names are absorbing the bulk of the pullback.

Broader sentiment gauges have moved with the tape: Fear & Greed-style readings have slipped into neutral-to-fear territory, down from greed levels seen earlier in the month, consistent with a real, if measured, risk-off shift rather than panic. Retail chatter is more stock-specific than directional — Nvidia, Alphabet and Apple are drawing bullish mention volume ahead of Nvidia's Wednesday earnings (options pricing a 5-7% move), alongside continued strength in Salesforce, CrowdStrike and Okta following last week's reports. That AI/software cluster holding up while chipmakers and rate-sensitive names lag suggests the pullback is being read as geopolitical and rate-driven rather than a broad loss of conviction in the earnings-led rally, though the signal leans more on price action and headlines than on any strong social-sentiment extreme today.
